_comment: Emirates NBD PJSC — FY2025 (year ended December 31, 2025)
_source: Emirates NBD FY2025 Press Release, emiratesnbd.com investor relations
_note_balance_sheet: Total Assets surpassed AED 1 trillion in 2025. Gross lending grew AED 129B (24%) to ~AED 669B. Deposits grew AED 119B (18%) to ~AED 779B. CASA AED 471B (60.5% of deposits). LDR 85.9%. UAE's largest bank by assets.
_note_deposits: CASA AED 471B = 60.5% of deposits. UAE has high CASA due to corporate current accounts (oil/trade) and retail savings. Current/Demand ~25%, Savings ~35%, Term ~40%.
_note_exposure: Corporate/Trade Finance ~45% (UAE is trade hub, large corporate book), Personal Banking ~25% (retail loans, credit cards), Mortgages ~20% (Dubai/UAE property market is active), SME ~10%.
_note_credit_quality: NPL improving trend; est. ~3.5% for FY2025 (Gulf banks carry higher NPLs than Singapore/US peers due to construction/real estate exposure and some SME stress). Emirates NBD has been on a multi-year improvement trajectory.
_note_pnl: Record PBT AED 29.8B. Total income AED 49.3B (+12%). NIM ~3.2% (guided 3.1-3.3% for 2026, FY2025 similar). ROA ~2.5% (UAE banks highly profitable — high rates + low opex + low tax). ROE ~20%. Cost-income ~35%.
_note_capital: CET1 14.4%, Total Capital 16.6% (Q4 2025). Well above UAE Central Bank requirements. UAE introduced 9% corporate tax in 2023 but banks remain highly profitable.
